summary: Dimdazenil (EVT-201) was evaluated for insomnia in a randomized clinical study at five U.S. sleep laboratories. Those study results are research findings, not U.S. marketing authorization. This entry has not verified an FDA-approved product label for dimdazenil; consult Drugs@FDA for current U.S. approval status.
dosageRemark: There is no verified U.S. FDA-approved dosing label for dimdazenil in this catalog entry. Doses used in U.S. or overseas clinical trials must not be treated as an FDA-approved prescription regimen. Confirm U.S. authorization through Drugs@FDA and obtain medical guidance rather than relying on research doses or foreign labeling.
generalRisks: A U.S. clinical study reported mostly mild or moderate adverse events and found a small decrease in next-morning digit-symbol test performance despite no significant increase in self-reported sleepiness. Do not assume driving or cognitive performance is unaffected. Alcohol, opioids and other sedatives may compound central nervous system depression.
saferUse: Verify approval and authorized labeling using the FDA's Drugs@FDA database before treating this investigational product as a U.S. prescription medicine.
Do not self-administer clinical-trial doses or foreign-approved regimens.
Avoid alcohol or combining with opioids and other sedatives without medical supervision, and do not drive while impaired.
